implementation_notes: The typed realization of the server-store architecture: @types/express-session augments Request with session, the stored shape is declared by augmenting SessionData in a .d.ts file, and the middleware plus store remain the manager and store roles. regenerate() on login and destroy() on logout are the policy calls. What replaces the classic structure is the typed middleware-plus-store combination; the remaining work is the SessionData declaration, cookie hardening and keeping the store out of the process for multi-instance deployment.
pitfalls: Without the declaration merge, req.session is untyped and property typos become silent runtime bugs; put SessionData in a .d.ts included by the compiler.
The callback API predates promises and does not compose with async handlers; wrap regenerate/destroy in promises or use a store facade that does.
The same MemoryStore trap as JavaScript applies: the default store is single-process and not production-ready.

variants.name: iron-session sealed cookie (stateless)
variants.implementation_notes: iron-session seals the session object itself into a signed and encrypted cookie, so there is no server store: getIronSession returns a typed facade (Node, Express, Connect, Next.js App Router) and save() rewrites the sealed cookie. This is the stateless realization - cheap to deploy, no store failure domain - but it cannot be centrally invalidated: logout clears the client cookie only, and a copied seal stays valid until ttl expires or the password is rotated. Choose it for small sessions (roughly 3 KB of data, single cookie) in Next.js-style deployments; choose the server-store variant when revocation, administrative logout or device management matters.
pitfalls: No server-side revocation: a copied cookie remains valid until ttl or password rotation, so logout cannot be absolute.
The 4 KB cookie limit and per-request header cost bound the payload; keep only an identifier and small facts, or use chunking deliberately.
Rotating the password invalidates every session at once, and unreadable cookies silently start empty sessions unless onUnsealError is logged.
